newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Tuesday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover fell to 2.8 billion yuan from 3.2 billion yuan on Monday, with the 60-day contract being the most active.
The falls on the domestic A share markets in both Shanghai and Shenzhen pulled borrowing down, said local traders.
Big state-owned banks traded little, waiting for the results of a national meeting of bankers which began in Beijing on Monday, they said.
"There were rumours on the market today that the central bank would ban commercial banks from trading on the T-bill repo market," a trader said. Officials declined to comment.
"If the rumours prove to be true, the ban will mean that the austerity measures in force since 1993 will continue," he added. "This is likely to support the rates in the short term."
